courseName: IB Environmental Systems and Societies SL
practices: Assessments evaluate core understanding in Environmental Systems and Societies. Focus on interdisciplinary thinking, systems thinking (inputs, outputs, stores, flows), and evaluating solutions.

units.unitTitle: Foundations of environmental systems and societies
keyTopics: Environmental value systems (EVS): ecocentric, anthropocentric, technocentric
Systems and models: open, closed, isolated systems
Energy and equilibria: laws of thermodynamics, stability
Species and populations, niche, carrying capacity
Flows of energy and matter, food chains, pyramids
An introduction to biodiversity: genetic, species, habitat
Origins of biodiversity, natural selection, plate tectonics
Threats to biodiversity, species extinction, red list

units.unitTitle: Water and aquatic food production systems
keyTopics: Water systems and resources, hydrological cycle
Access to fresh water, water conservation

units.unitTitle: Soil systems and terrestrial food production
keyTopics: Introduction to soil systems, soil profile, horizons
Terrestrial food production systems and food choices

examFormat.freeResponse: Paper 2: Short-answer and structured essays (70%), 2 hours

antiPatterns: Avoid HL extension topics under all circumstances. Never ask questions about: environmental economics (e.g., circular economy details) or advanced ethical systems (1.5), complex population dynamics modeling formulas (2.1), and global environmental international policy histories (5.4). Keep systems thinking simple and conceptual.
